fieldData.post-body:
This (1) article is designed to help you, the content creator, uncover the best tool for harnessing authentic user queries, filling content gaps, and elevating your SEO strategy.

Every creator faces the challenge of finding the right questions to answer—questions that resonate with your audience and drive meaningful engagement.

In this guide, we explore two popular keyword research tools, AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic, and explain how each can reveal hidden content opportunities, boost your SEO performance, and strengthen your online authority.

Why Understanding User Queries Matters

Understanding what your audience is asking is the cornerstone of creating impactful content.

In my experience, leveraging real user queries has significantly improved click-through rates and boosted organic traffic, sometimes by as much as 20-30% and 25% respectively, although individual results will always vary.

When you directly address user questions, you not only build trust but also enhance your site’s click-through rates and organic traffic.

Here's an example of the organic traffic boost one of my articles experienced after using AlsoAsked.

In this and the following examples, I’m using real data from my work on an article about how to make money on Fansly.

Getting to Know AlsoAsked

What Is AlsoAsked and How Does It Work?

AlsoAsked is a tool designed to extract questions from Google’s “People Also Ask” section.

By mining these real user queries, it delivers a wealth of long-tail keyword ideas and uncovers content gaps.

This helps you craft posts, FAQs, or even entire course modules that directly answer what your audience is curious about.

How AlsoAsked Extracts Google’s People Also Ask

AlsoAsked queries Google and captures the “People Also Ask” data in a structured way.

This process lets you:

  • Extract a hierarchy of related questions
  • Visualize clusters of similar queries
  • Export findings in CSV format for deeper analysis

This structured extraction means you can see how one question naturally leads to another—a conversation you can mirror in your content.

Key Functionalities of AlsoAsked

AlsoAsked offers a range of features designed to streamline your content research:

  • Data Visualization: Clear visual maps of related questions highlight content opportunities at a glance.
  • Clustering: Similar questions are grouped together, enabling you to cover topics comprehensively.

Understanding AnswerThePublic

What Is AnswerThePublic and How Does It Work?

AnswerThePublic takes a different approach by using Google autocomplete data to generate question maps and keyword ideas.

It captures common search queries as you type and transforms them into a visual representation of topics and subtopics.

This broader view can spark a range of content ideas beyond the specific queries found in People Also Ask.

Unique Features of AnswerThePublic

AnswerThePublic offers several distinct features:

  • Visual Question Maps: Organized layouts of questions and phrases help you see potential topics and subtopics instantly.
  • Keyword Ideation: In addition to questions, it suggests related keywords to bolster your overall SEO strategy.

You can also view the results in AnswerThePublic using the table view.

Data Sources and Methodologies: A Comparative Look

How the Tools Source Their Data

Both tools offer valuable insights, but they use different data sources:

AlsoAsked

  • Sources data from Google’s People Also Ask
  • Focuses on real, user-asked questions for pinpoint content gaps

AnswerThePublic

  • Uses Google autocomplete data
  • Captures a broader variety of queries, resulting in a wider scope of keyword ideas

Impact of Methodology on Insights

The different data sources influence the insights each tool provides:

  • AlsoAsked yields highly targeted, long-tail questions that help fill specific content gaps.
  • AnswerThePublic offers a broader array of ideas, making it ideal for brainstorming and identifying trending topics.

User Interface and Workflow Efficiency

  • May feel more overwhelming if you need precise, targeted data
In my workflow, I often start with AlsoAsked to drill down on exact queries, then use AnswerThePublic to supplement with broader trends.

Which Tool Fits Your Content Strategy?

Tailoring Your Choice to Your Needs

The choice between tools depends on your specific content goals:

  • If you need detailed, niche topics: AlsoAsked is ideal for uncovering specific user queries.
  • If you need broad inspiration: AnswerThePublic is perfect for generating diverse content ideas across various formats.

Actionable Insights for Different Strategies

Consider your content format:

  • Multi-language Blogs: The precision of AlsoAsked can help tailor content to different language audiences.
  • Video Tutorials and Courses: AnswerThePublic’s visual maps can serve as a creative tool to structure your video or course modules around trending questions.

Both tools empower you to build stronger topical authority by ensuring your content directly addresses your audience’s needs.

For a deeper dive into content optimization, check out my guide on SEO for Beginners.

Use Cases: AlsoAsked vs. AnswerThePublic for Different Creators

Fitness YouTuber

AlsoAsked

A fitness YouTuber creating content about "at-home workouts" could use AlsoAsked to find specific questions like:

  • "What are the best at-home workouts for beginners?"
  • "How to do at-home workouts without equipment?"
  • "What are effective at-home workouts for weight loss?"
  • "What is the best time for at home workout?"
  • "What are good at home workouts to build muscle?"

This helps them create highly targeted videos that address specific audience concerns, potentially leading to a series of videos on "At-Home Workouts for Beginners," "No-Equipment Workouts," etc.

AnswerThePublic

The same YouTuber could use AnswerThePublic to brainstorm broader content ideas around "fitness" or "workout routines."

This could lead to videos on:

  • "Are short workouts effective?"
  • "How to stay motivated to workout?"
  • "Which workout routine is best for me?"
  • "When to do cardio vs. strength training?"

These broader topics can attract a wider audience and help establish the YouTuber as a fitness authority.

If you're a YouTube creator, check out my guide on leveraging YouTube-specific tools to generate content ideas and boost SEO—VidIQ vs. TubeBuddy.

Affiliate Marketer Promoting Travel Gear

AlsoAsked

‍An affiliate marketer promoting travel gear on a blog or website could use AlsoAsked to discover questions like, for example:

  • "How to choose the best travel backpack?"
  • "What is the best way to pack a suitcase efficiently?"
  • "How to clean a travel backpack?"
  • "What are the most durable travel accessories?"
  • "Where to buy reliable travel gear online?"

They could then create in-depth blog posts, reviews, or comparison guide that answer these questions, naturally weaving in their affiliate links to relevant products.

For more tips on optimizing your affiliate content strategy, check out my guide on affiliate marketing for creators.

AnswerThePublic

‍The same affiliate marketer could use AnswerThePublic to explore broader topics around "travel packing tips" or "best travel gear."

Resulting in content like:

  • "What are the essential items for carry-on luggage?"
  • "Which travel gadgets are actually worth buying?"
  • "How to pack for a backpacking trip?"
  • "Why is it important to have travel insurance?"
  • "Will this backpack be allowed as carry-on?"

This helps them attract a wider audience interested in travel preparation, providing ample opportunities to promote relevant affiliate products.

To discover creative ideas for affiliate content and learn how to choose the right products to promote, see my guides on finding ideas for affiliate content and choosing affiliate products.

Online Course Creator (Photography)

AlsoAsked

A course creator teaching "beginner photography" could use AlsoAsked to find questions like, for example:

  • "What are the best camera settings for beginner photographers?"
  • "How to take good photos with a smartphone?"
  • "What is aperture in photography?"
  • "How does ISO affect photo quality?"

These questions could directly inform the content of their course modules, ensuring they address common beginner struggles.

AnswerThePublic

The same creator could use AnswerThePublic to explore broader topics around "photography techniques" or "photo editing."

  • "How to edit photos like a professional?"
  • "Which photography techniques are best for landscapes?"
  • "Why are my photos blurry?"
  • "What is the best photography style?"

These broader topics could inspire bonus modules, blog posts, or even ideas for future courses, expanding their reach and authority.

Once you've identified the key questions and content gaps, remember that if you're creating content for social media, it's important not only to address those gaps but also to optimize your posts for reach.

For actionable tips, check out my guide on hashtags for creators.

Implementing Actionable Insights into Your Content Planning

Step-by-Step Integration Example

Here’s how I integrate these tools into my content workflow:

  1. Identify Core Questions: Enter a broad topic into AlsoAsked to extract a list of specific user queries.
  2. Visual Brainstorming: Use AnswerThePublic to create a visual map of related topics, inspiring ideas for blog posts, videos, or course modules.
  3. Cluster and Prioritize: Group similar questions together. Focus on those that are most relevant to your audience and align with your expertise.
  4. Content Creation: Structure your content around these clusters. Consider building an FAQ section or dedicating individual posts to the most common questions.
  5. Validate with Analytics: After publishing, monitor performance using tools like Google Analytics. Adjust your strategy based on the data to continuously improve your content.

Integrating these steps ensures that your content is both data-driven and genuinely helpful to your audience.

Additionally, AI tools like ChatGPT can help turn these questions into actionable outlines.

Case Study: Boosting Engagement with User-Driven Content

In a recent project, I discovered a niche cluster of questions using AlsoAsked.

I structured a blog post around these queries and supplemented it with broader insights from AnswerThePublic.

The result was a significant increase in organic traffic and higher engagement from readers who appreciated the depth of the answers provided.

By tapping into the authentic questions my audience was asking, I was able to create content that resonated deeply and improved the my site’s SEO performance.

This experience confirms that combining targeted and broad keyword research can transform your content strategy.

Exploring Alternative Keyword Research Tools

A Broader Look at the Keyword Landscape

While AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic are powerful, there are several other tools that might complement your strategy:

  • KeywordsPeopleUse: Focuses on generating long-tail keyword ideas using natural language queries.
  • Frase: Combines keyword research with content optimization by providing actionable briefs.
  • Ubersuggest & KWFinder: Offer extensive keyword data along with competitive analysis.
  • SEMrush & Ahrefs: Provide robust, data-driven insights ideal for larger agencies or creators with comprehensive SEO needs.

When to Consider These Alternatives

If your content strategy requires both deep query analysis and a broader keyword view, consider integrating these tools.

For example, while AlsoAsked pinpoints specific questions, SEMrush or Ahrefs can provide detailed competitive insights and search volume data for a more rounded approach.

Creator Clarity Checkpoint

Before finalizing your content plan, ask yourself:

  • Have I identified the core questions my audience is asking?
  • Does my content address these questions in a clear, structured manner?
  • Have I integrated insights from multiple tools to build a robust strategy?
  • Am I tracking performance with analytics to iterate and improve?

This checkpoint helps ensure your content not only fills existing gaps but also evolves alongside your audience’s needs.

Final Thoughts and Next Steps

Choosing the right tool depends on your unique content goals.

Whether you lean toward the precision of AlsoAsked or the broad ideation offered by AnswerThePublic, each tool delivers actionable insights that can elevate your SEO strategy and build your authority online.

In my experience, blending both approaches has resulted in content that truly resonates—leading to increased traffic and deeper reader trust.

As you refine your content process, experiment with both tools and consider integrating alternative keyword research platforms to cover every angle.

Your Next Steps

  1. Experiment: Start by using AlsoAsked to gather real user questions for your next blog post or course module.
  2. Visualize: Use AnswerThePublic to brainstorm additional content ideas and visualize trending topics.
  3. Integrate: Combine insights from both tools with data from Google Analytics to refine your SEO strategy.
  4. Optimize: Monitor your content’s performance, iterate based on what resonates most with your audience, and keep refining your approach.

By following these steps, you’re not just collecting data—you’re building a content strategy that drives engagement, fosters trust, and ultimately helps you monetize your expertise.

Happy creating!

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
fieldData.faq:
Can I use AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic for keyword research in languages other than English?

Yes, both AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic support keyword research in multiple languages. AlsoAsked allows you to select the specific language and region you want to target, while AnswerThePublic offers a dropdown menu to choose your desired language during the search process. This makes them valuable tools for creating multilingual content and reaching a global audience.

How often is the data updated on AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic?

AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic rely on real-time data from Google. AlsoAsked scrapes data from Google's People Also Ask section, and AnswerThePublic uses Google's autocomplete suggestions. Thus, the results you see are based on current search trends. However, the frequency with which Google updates its data can influence the freshness of the results.

Can I use AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic for local SEO?

Yes, both tools can be helpful for local SEO. AlsoAsked allows you to choose a specific region along with the language, enabling you to find hyper-local results. AnswerThePublic helps you identify locally relevant keywords and questions by analyzing Google Autocomplete suggestions, which are often influenced by the searcher's location. By combining the insights from both tools, you can tailor your content to target a specific geographic area.

Are there any browser extensions for AlsoAsked or AnswerThePublic?

While AlsoAsked doesn't have a dedicated browser extension, AnswerThePublic was acquired by Neil Patel and is available as a part of the Ubersuggest extension. This allows you to perform keyword research and access AnswerThePublic's data directly within your browser while searching on Google. Keep in mind that some features may require a paid Ubersuggest subscription.

How do AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic compare to the "Searches related to" section at the bottom of Google's results?

AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic offer a more structured and comprehensive approach compared to the "Searches related to" section. AlsoAsked provides a hierarchical view of related questions, showing the connections between them, while "Searches related to" offers a simple list. AnswerThePublic offers broader ideation, going beyond questions to present related prepositions, comparisons, and more in a visual format. In short, these tools provide a deeper and more organized way to understand search intent.

Can I use AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic for YouTube keyword research?

While neither tool is specifically designed for YouTube, you can adapt the results for video keyword research. AlsoAsked's questions are very useful for structuring video content and addressing specific audience queries. AnswerThePublic's broader keyword suggestions can inspire video ideas and help you optimize video titles and descriptions. It's a great starting point, but remember to further refine your research using YouTube-specific tools. Also you can use KeywordsPeopleUse that uses Youtube as a data source.

What is the difference between "questions," "prepositions," and "comparisons" in AnswerThePublic?

AnswerThePublic categorizes its results to provide different perspectives on search intent. "Questions" are queries phrased as questions (who, what, where, when, why, how). "Prepositions" show searches that include prepositions like "for," "with," "to," or "without," revealing relationships between keywords. "Comparisons" display searches that compare things, often using words like "vs," "or," "and." These different categories help you understand the nuances of how people search for information related to your topic.

Can I integrate AlsoAsked or AnswerThePublic with other SEO tools?

AlsoAsked primarily integrates with CSV, allowing for data export that can be used in various SEO tools. AnswerThePublic being acquired by Neil Patel and now part of the Ubersuggest ecosystem can be used together. You can also manually transfer data from both tools into other SEO platforms for further analysis, such as combining question research with keyword volume data from tools like SEMrush or Ahrefs.

How reliable are AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic for predicting future trends?

Both tools reflect current search behavior, but they don't directly predict future trends. AlsoAsked reflects questions that users are already asking in Google's "People Also Ask" section. AnswerThePublic's reliance on Google Autocomplete also means it's based on existing search patterns. While they can provide hints about emerging interests, it is recommended to combine their insights with other trend analysis tools for a more comprehensive view of future trends.

What are some tips for using AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic most effectively?

Start with a broad keyword to get a wide range of ideas, then use AlsoAsked to drill down into specific questions and AnswerThePublic to brainstorm related topics. Combine the insights from both tools with your own audience knowledge and other keyword research tools for a well-rounded strategy. Regularly revisit your research to stay updated with evolving search trends and audience interests. Using AI tools like ChatGPT can also help you turn the questions found into actionable content outlines and drafts.

What Is a Hashtag?

A hashtag is a word or phrase preceded by the # symbol.

Hashtags simplify content discovery on social media and have become a powerful promotional tool.

For instance, Instagram posts with at least one hashtag get 12.6% more engagement compared to posts without them.

In 2024, the hashtag #TravelTuesday inspired thousands to share their travel adventures, boosting the popularity of travel content and increasing bookings.

However, how hashtags work changes every year.

If you create content—blogs, illustrations, designs, or educational videos—it's important to understand how hashtags work in 2025. Let’s explore how to get the most out of them.

The Evolution of Hashtags

In 2007, hashtags first appeared on Twitter as a way to organize conversations. They quickly became a tool for joining global discussions, tracking trends, and amplifying content reach.

Following their success on Twitter, hashtags spread to Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn, adapting to each platform’s unique needs:

  1. Instagram: For discovering new content and improving visibility.
  2. Facebook: For grouping discussions and events.
  3. LinkedIn: For professional networking and visibility.

Content creators actively use hashtags to attract audiences, increase reach, and spark viral trends.

How Hashtags Work in 2026

Instagram: From Quantity to Quality

Hashtags on Instagram remain important, but the focus has shifted to relevance.

  • Targeted hashtags work better than generic ones. For example, #WatercolorArtists attracts more attention than #Art.
  • Instagram’s algorithm promotes posts with hashtags that match users’ recent interests, such as #EcoFriendlyArt.
  • Where Do Hashtags Go on Instagram? Add them to captions or comments to improve readability and avoid visual clutter.

A Case of a Successful Branded Hashtag

I assisted in developing social media for the artist Anna Lomakina.

She had a YouTube channel with 300,000 subscribers, but her Instagram was growing slowly.

We came up with the hashtag #ломакина_глянь.

At the end of her videos, Anya would give viewers a drawing challenge.

They would post their work on Instagram using this hashtag to be featured in her next video, where she showcased the best results.

Result: Over 150,000 works were published under this hashtag, and Anya's account grew from 10,000 to 100,000 followers in a short period.

TikTok: Trends and Communities

On TikTok, hashtags help users discover content and form communities.

  • Communities: For example, #BookTok united book lovers and influenced bestseller lists.
  • Viral Tags: Hashtags like #DanceChallenge generate high engagement.
  • What Hashtags to Use on TikTok: Mix trending and niche hashtags, such as #SmallCreators, to broaden your reach.

X (formerly Twitter): Real-Time Discussions

Hashtags on X are key to joining live events and trending conversations.

  • Use them to search topics and increase tweet visibility.
  • Add hashtags strategically to stay at the center of relevant discussions.

LinkedIn: Building Professional Reputation

LinkedIn relies on precise hashtag use for professional networking.

  • Industry-Specific Tags: Hashtags like #DigitalMarketing help connect with colleagues.
  • Professional Trends: Showcase your expertise with relevant hashtags but avoid overloading posts.

Hashtags and SEO: How They’re Connected

Hashtags on social media function like keywords in SEO. They simplify searches and help users find your content.

  • Aligning hashtags with your SEO strategy increases visibility.
  • Choose hashtags relevant to popular topics and audience interests.
  • Branded hashtags create a cohesive and recognizable image.

Reach on Platforms and Beyond

Hashtags are highly effective within apps but have limited impact on external search engines like Google.

  1. Within Platforms: Help users find your content faster.
  2. Beyond Platforms: Use broader SEO strategies to improve your Google ranking.

Free Tools to Find the Best Hashtags

Effective hashtag selection can be challenging, but these tools can help:

  1. Ahrefs Free AI Instagram Hashtag Generator: Generates hashtags optimized for your content.
  2. KeywordTool.io: Helps find hashtags for platforms like Instagram and Twitter.
  3. AnswerThePublic or AlsoAsked: Suggests unique hashtags based on popular user searches. Check out my guide and comparison of AlsoAsked and AnswerThePublic.
  4. VidIQ or TubeBuddy: These powerful YouTube SEO tools not only optimize your videos but also help uncover effective hashtags. For more tips on leveraging these tools, check out my guide on YouTube SEO strategies.

Conclusion: Are Hashtags Still Relevant?

Hashtags remain a crucial tool for promotion when used thoughtfully.

  • Consider the unique dynamics of each platform.
  • Combine trending and evergreen hashtags.
  • Use analytical tools to refine your strategy.

fieldData.faq:
Are hashtags still relevant on social media in 2026?

Yes, hashtags are still a valuable tool for content discovery and promotion. Platforms like Instagram and TikTok rely heavily on targeted hashtags, while others like Facebook see diminishing effectiveness. Tailoring your strategy to the platform is key.

What are the best tools to generate hashtags?

Tools like Ahrefs' Free AI Instagram Hashtag Generator and KeywordTool.io can help you find relevant hashtags. Additionally, AnswerThePublic offers audience-driven suggestions based on popular searches.

What hashtags are trending on TikTok right now?

Trending TikTok hashtags frequently change, but a mix of viral tags such as #DanceChallenge and niche tags like #SmallCreators can maximize engagement. Check TikTok’s Explore page regularly for updates.

How many hashtags should I use on Instagram?

For Instagram, quality is more important than quantity. Using 5–10 highly relevant hashtags in captions or comments can boost visibility without overwhelming your content.

Can I use spaces or punctuation in hashtags?

No, hashtags cannot contain spaces or most punctuation marks. Use letters, numbers, or underscores only, for example, #BestTravelMoments.

What’s the difference between trending and niche hashtags?

Trending hashtags target a broader audience and can quickly increase visibility, while niche hashtags connect with specific communities. A mix of both provides the best results.

How can I create unique wedding hashtags?

Combine personal elements like names, dates, and themes to craft creative hashtags, such as #SmithWedding2025. Wedding hashtag generators are also a great resource for unique ideas.

Can hashtags improve SEO for my content?

On social media, hashtags function similarly to keywords by enhancing discoverability. However, their impact on external search engines like Google is limited, so focus primarily on in-platform optimization.

What are the best hashtags for Instagram in 2025?

The most effective hashtags are targeted and specific, like #EcoFriendlyArt for sustainable content or #FoodieLife for culinary topics. Prioritize relevance to your audience and content.

How do I avoid getting shadowbanned for hashtags?

Avoid banned or irrelevant hashtags, as these can harm your visibility. Research your hashtags carefully and ensure they align with your content to maintain a healthy reach.

fieldData.post-body:
No one knows if llms.txt actually works—but here's why I use it anyway, and what happened when I added it to my sites.

In September 2024, AI researcher Jeremy Howard proposed a simple idea: give AI systems a clean map of your website's best content. The file is called llms.txt, and it's supposed to help ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and other AI tools understand what your site is about.

I've implemented llms.txt on my own multilingual blog and for clients like united24media.com. The results? Modest but noticeable AI traffic increases—and one site saw +113% traffic in 30 days.

But here's the thing: I can't prove llms.txt caused any of it.

This guide covers what llms.txt actually is, the honest evidence for and against it, and step-by-step implementation for Webflow and WordPress creators.

What is llms.txt?

llms.txt is a simple text file that sits at your website's root (yoursite.com/llms.txt) and tells AI systems what your most important content is.

Think of it as a curated menu for AI crawlers.

While robots.txt tells search engines what they can't access, llms.txt tells AI systems what content is most useful.

It's written in Markdown format—plain text that AI systems process more efficiently than messy HTML full of navigation menus and ads.

‍

The specification was created by Jeremy Howard, co-founder of Answer.AI and former president of Kaggle. His credentials matter: he pioneered transfer learning techniques that contributed to models like GPT. When someone this accomplished proposes a standard, the tech world pays attention.

Here's what a basic llms.txt file looks like:

# Your Site Name
> A one-sentence description of what you do and who you help.
## Main Content
- [Your Best Guide](https://yoursite.com/guide): What this page covers
- [Popular Article](https://yoursite.com/article): Why it's valuable
## Optional
- [Blog Archive](https://yoursite.com/blog): Secondary content

The only required element is the H1 heading with your site name. Everything else—descriptions, link sections, the "Optional" marker—helps AI systems but isn't mandatory.

Here's my llms.txt in action:

Does llms.txt actually work?

Let's be honest: the evidence is genuinely mixed.

What the research says

No major AI company has confirmed they use llms.txt.‍

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Perplexity have all published their own llms.txt files for documentation sites—but none have stated their AI systems read llms.txt files from other websites.

Google's John Mueller compared llms.txt to the "keywords meta tag"—a deprecated standard no search engine uses anymore. He stated: "None of the AI services have said they're using LLMs.txt... and you can tell when you look at your server logs that they don't even check for it."

When website owners check their server logs, results are thin.

SE Ranking's study of 300,000 domains found no correlation between AI citations and llms.txt implementation.

Semrush tested directly: over two months, they observed zero visits from GPTBot, ClaudeBot, or PerplexityBot to llms.txt files.

What I've seen in practice

My experience tells a slightly different story—though I'm careful about claiming causation.

After adding llms.txt to my multilingual blog (English, Ukrainian, Russian), I noticed AI tools started sending more traffic to my English articles specifically. The effect wasn't dramatic, but it was measurable. My theory: the llms.txt file helped AI systems understand which language versions to prioritize.

For a client site—united24media.com—we saw +113% traffic increase in 30 days after implementing llms.txt alongside other optimizations.

Was it the llms.txt file?

Impossible to isolate. But the timing was interesting.

Here's my honest assessment:

‍llms.txt is a helper, not a magic solution. If your content isn't great, llms.txt won't save you. If your content is already good, llms.txt might give AI systems the context they need to find and cite it.

Why implement it anyway?

The risk-reward calculation is simple:

  • Downside: 30 minutes of work
  • Upside: If AI providers eventually adopt the standard, you're already positioned

Over 13,000 websites have implemented llms.txt, with adoption growing roughly 600% between February and May 2025. Notable adopters include Anthropic, Cloudflare, Stripe, and Zapier—all for developer documentation.

For creators targeting developer audiences or using AI coding assistants like Cursor (which explicitly supports llms.txt), the value is clearer. For general content creators, it's a calculated bet on an uncertain standard.

How to create an llms.txt file

Creating your llms.txt file takes about 30 minutes and requires no coding knowledge.

Step 1: Identify your best content

Start by listing your 10-20 most important pages:

  • Your about page
  • Key product or service pages
  • FAQ sections
  • Your best-performing blog posts
  • Any cornerstone content

Don't include your entire site. The point is curation, not completeness.

Step 2: Write the file

Open any text editor and create this structure:

# [Your Site Name]

> [One sentence: What you do + who you help]

[2-3 sentences of additional context about your expertise or approach]

## Core Content
- [Homepage](https://yoursite.com): [What visitors learn here]
- [About](https://yoursite.com/about): [Your background and story]
- [Services](https://yoursite.com/services): [What you offer]

## Resources
- [Best Guide](https://yoursite.com/guide): [Why it's valuable]
- [Popular Article](https://yoursite.com/article): [Key takeaway]

## Optional
- [Blog](https://yoursite.com/blog): [What topics you cover]
- [Contact](https://yoursite.com/contact): [How to reach you]

Step 3: Make descriptions specific

This is where most people fail. Generic descriptions waste your optimization opportunity.

Weak:

[Marketing Services](https://yoursite.com/services): Marketing help

Strong:

[Marketing Services](https://yoursite.com/services): Digital marketing for local restaurants—Google Business Profile optimization, review management, and local SEO

The more specific your descriptions, the better AI systems can match relevant queries.

Step 4: Keep it concise

Keep the file under 3,000 words. AI systems may skip overly long files. Quality over quantity.

Step 5: Validate before publishing

Use free validators to catch errors:

  • llmstxtvalidator.dev
  • llmstxtchecker.net

Check for missing H1 headings, broken links, or formatting issues.

How to add llms.txt to Webflow

Webflow now offers native support for llms.txt.

Method 1: Using the SEO field (recommended)

  1. Go to Site Settings → SEO in your Webflow dashboard
  2. Look for the llms.txt field (Webflow added this dedicated field recently)
  3. Paste your llms.txt content directly
  4. Publish your site

The file will be served from yoursite.com/llms.txt automatically.

Method 2: Using Assets Panel

  1. Create your llms.txt file locally
  2. Go to the Assets Panel in Webflow
  3. Upload the file
  4. Webflow will serve it from your domain root

I use Method 1 because it's easier to update directly in the dashboard without re-uploading files.

How to add llms.txt to WordPress

WordPress has several options depending on your preferred workflow.

Using Yoast SEO (easiest)

If you already use Yoast SEO, they added one-click llms.txt generation in June 2025:

  1. Go to Yoast SEO → Settings → Site Features
  2. Toggle on the llms.txt option
  3. The plugin auto-generates your file weekly, prioritizing cornerstone content

The auto-generated version is a decent starting point, but you may want to customize descriptions for better results.

Using a dedicated plugin

The "Website LLMs.txt" plugin offers more control:

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Go to Settings → LLMs.txt
  3. Write or paste your custom llms.txt content
  4. Save

Manual upload

If you prefer full control:

  1. Create your llms.txt file locally
  2. Connect via FTP or your hosting file manager
  3. Upload to your site's root directory (same folder as wp-config.php)

Common mistakes to avoid

Making the file too long

If your llms.txt is 10,000 words, you've defeated the purpose. AI systems have limited context windows. Include only content that genuinely matters.

Wrong file location

Your file must live at exactly yoursite.com/llms.txt—not in a subdirectory. AI crawlers look for it at the root.

Vague descriptions

"Great content for entrepreneurs" tells AI nothing useful. Specific details about what each page covers help AI systems match relevant queries.

Forgetting to update

If your llms.txt links to pages that no longer exist, AI systems may lose trust in your site's reliability. Schedule quarterly reviews.

Including low-value pages

Exclude checkout flows, user account pages, tag archives, and anything behind authentication. Focus on your best public content.

What about llms-full.txt?

A variant called llms-full.txt contains complete content rather than just links. It was developed by Mintlify in collaboration with Anthropic.

The idea: instead of making AI systems follow URLs to get content, give them everything directly. This is useful for documentation sites where you want AI to have immediate access.

For most content creators, the standard llms.txt with links is sufficient. Use llms-full.txt only if you specifically want AI systems to have your complete content without crawling.

Alternatives that definitely work today

While llms.txt remains speculative, proven AI optimization methods exist:

Structured data (Schema.org)

Schema markup helps AI systems understand your content's context—what type it is, who created it, when it was published. Unlike llms.txt, structured data is actively used by Google's AI systems. Add FAQ schema, Article schema, and HowTo schema where relevant.

Answer-first content structure

AI systems love content that directly answers questions. Start each section with a clear answer in 40-60 words, then expand. This structure helps both AI Overviews and traditional featured snippets.

Traditional SEO excellence

Many AI tools pull answers from search results. The same SEO fundamentals that help Google understand your content—clean heading hierarchy, short paragraphs, direct answers—also help AI systems find your best work.

The bottom line

llms.txt is a 30-minute investment with uncertain but potentially significant upside. No major AI company has confirmed they use it, but adoption is growing and the specification comes from a credible source.

My approach: implement it, but don't obsess over it. The file takes minimal effort to create and maintain. If AI providers eventually standardize on llms.txt, you'll be ahead. If they don't, you've lost almost nothing.

Focus on what definitely works—great content, clear structure, proper schema markup—and treat llms.txt as one small piece of your AI discoverability strategy. That's all!

Frequently Asked Questions
fieldData.faq:
Do AI crawlers actually read llms.txt files?

No major AI company has confirmed their systems read llms.txt. Server log analyses show mixed results—some sites report increased AI crawler activity, others see no change. The honest answer: we don't know for certain.

Is llms.txt the same as robots.txt?

No. robots.txt tells crawlers what they can't access. llms.txt tells AI systems what content is most useful—it's curation, not restriction. They serve different purposes and both can exist on your site.

Should I implement llms.txt if I'm just starting out?

If your content isn't great yet, llms.txt won't help. Focus on creating genuinely useful content first. Once you have 10-20 strong pages worth curating, then consider llms.txt.

How often should I update my llms.txt file?

Review quarterly, or whenever you publish major new content. Remove broken links and add your newest important pages. Outdated llms.txt files with dead links may hurt more than help.

Does llms.txt help with Google rankings?

Google has explicitly stated they don't use llms.txt and have no plans to support it. llms.txt is for AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity—not traditional search engines.

fieldData.post-body:
I’ve been running this blog for 10 years, and 95% of my traffic comes from search engines. 

Over the past year, the site has been visited by 270,000 people.

The screenshot shows that on January 3, 2024, there were only 74 clicks from search, but by December 18, 2024, the number grew to 2,700.

This happened despite moving from Tilda to Webflow, adding new languages, and experiencing a temporary drop in traffic.

SEO has helped me attract readers who find my articles and generate income through affiliate marketing.

Right now, a lot is changing due to artificial intelligence.

In this article, I’ll share my experience and ideas on how to start getting traffic through SEO.

What is SEO?

Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is a way to make your content more visible online.

Thanks to SEO, you can attract free visitors without spending money on ads.

If people search for something, SEO helps make sure they find your content more often.

How Does Search Engine Optimization Work?

You need to choose the right keywords for titles and descriptions, create attractive visuals, and ensure your site is free of technical errors.

It’s also important to have other quality resources link to your site—this shows search engines that your content is trustworthy.

Whether you’re optimizing for search engines, social media, or marketplaces, the steps are generally the same:

1. Analyze User Intent

People search for information with different goals: to learn something new, compare products or services, or find a specific product to buy.

It’s important to determine what task your content solves and adapt it to the user’s intent.

For example, if you’re comparing donation platforms like Patreon and Buy Me a Coffee, don’t optimize your article for keywords like “patreon site” or “patreon support.”

These queries are made by people who already know about the platform and are looking for official resources.

Your content won’t be helpful for them.

Instead, focus on keywords reflecting comparison or choice: “best donation platforms” or “Patreon vs. Buy Me a Coffee.”

How to Analyze Intent

  1. Study search queries: Use tools like Google Keyword Planner to understand what phrases people type into search engines.
  2. Review search results: Look at what types of content (articles, videos, reviews) Google displays for a given query.
  3. Analyze competitors: Check how competitors solve users’ problems in their materials.

How to Determine Intent Type

Search queries can be divided into:

  1. Informational: The user wants to learn something new (“what are donations”).
  2. Navigational: The user looks for a specific resource (“login to Buy Me a Coffee”).
  3. Transactional: The user is ready to buy or register for something (“how to create a Patreon account”).

Understanding user intent helps create content that precisely meets their needs and increases your chances of success.

2. Keyword Research

Once you’ve identified user intent, it’s important to find out which keywords they use to search for content.

At the beginning, it’s better to target long-tail keywords because they have less competition.

For example, creating a popular article for the query “how to set up a Patreon subscription for artists” is easier than targeting a broader keyword like “Patreon registration.”

How to Analyze Keywords

There are paid services like SE Ranking, Ahrefs, and Semrush.

These tools allow you to:

  1. Enter a keyword, select a country, and see how often it’s searched.
  2. Determine the level of competition and the quality of existing content on the topic.
  3. See which websites rank at the top.
  4. Discover additional questions users ask related to that keyword.

In the bottom-right corner, you can see that the difficulty of the keyword “what is Patreon” is 66, while “what's Patreon” is only 17.

This internal metric shows how hard it is to rank at the top for these queries.

Although higher-volume keywords can drive more traffic, it’s better to start with niche queries.

If your content is high-quality, you can eventually compete in more popular topics.

How to Identify Topic Popularity for Free

In our article on finding content ideas for affiliate marketing, we’ve already mentioned AnswerThePublic and ChatGPT.

Let’s also consider Google Trends:

  1. Google Trends: Allows you to select a topic, country, and time frame to see how popular it is. It also highlights related topics that might interest your audience and inspire new content ideas.
  2. AnswerThePublic and AlsoAsked: Provides deeper insights into user interests. Simply enter a keyword, select your country and language, and you’ll receive a list of the questions people are asking on search engines. For more details, check out the comparison between AnswerThePublic and AlsoAsked.
  3. ChatGPT: Helps brainstorm and analyze content ideas. It’s a tool I use daily. Learn more about working with ChatGPT here.

These tools can help you create a content plan and decide which topics to cover.

These tools can help you create a content plan and decide which topics to cover.

How to Start SEO?

The specifics of optimization depend on the platform you’re publishing on.

The main rule is to create content for people, not search engines. It should be clear, engaging, and easy to consume.

In the past, getting to the top could be achieved by using tricks like keyword stuffing and placement.

Today, this approach no longer works.

Here are some basic recommendations:

1. For Search Engines (Google, Bing, Perplexity)

To make your website more discoverable:

  1. Use keywords naturally: Add them to titles, descriptions, and text as part of natural speech. Instead of repeating “Patreon registration”, use variations like “register on Patreon” or “create a Patreon account.”
  2. Create useful content: Write articles or make videos that directly answer users’ queries. Start with narrow topics that have low competition.
  3. Focus on technical aspects: If you have your own site, check its loading speed, fix errors, and ensure it’s mobile-friendly.
  4. Build trust: Aim to get links to your site from other quality resources.

These steps will help your site rank higher in search results.

2. For Social Media (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest)

To boost your content in social recommendations, start by creating clear, precise titles and pairing them with engaging descriptions and quality thumbnails.

With advances in AI, hashtags are becoming less crucial, as platforms now analyze your video content directly and serve it to the right audiences.

This evolution means you can spend less time on technical tweaks and more on producing quality content.

Plus, each platform offers its own tools for spotting trends and analyzing keywords—on YouTube, for example, a simple keyword search can reveal what’s currently capturing viewers' interest.

For more insights into how advanced YouTube SEO tools can elevate your content, check out my guide on optimizing YouTube with VidIQ.

3. For Marketplaces (Etsy, Shutterstock, Gumroad)

To make your products or work more discoverable:

  1. Write accurate and detailed descriptions, including keywords users might type.
  2. Use quality images to catch attention.
  3. Adapt to the platform’s specifics: for example, on Etsy, unique details matter, while on Shutterstock, precise keywords for photos are key.
I’m working on detailed guides for SEO on each platform.

4. Technical Optimization

Technical optimization ensures your site is user-friendly and attractive to search engines.

Here are the key aspects:

  1. Loading speed: Ensure your site loads quickly. Slow pages deter visitors and hurt your search rankings.
  2. Mobile version: Make sure your site is mobile-friendly, as most users browse on their phones.
  3. URL structure: Use short and clear URLs with keywords. For example, instead of “site.com/page123,” use “site.com/how-to-optimize-seo.”
  4. Fix errors: Check for broken links (404 errors) and other issues. Free tools like Screaming Frog can help diagnose problems.
  5. Security: Install an SSL certificate to ensure your site uses HTTPS, which increases trust from both users and search engines.

Good website builders like Webflow or Weblium handle most of these tasks automatically.

To analyze technical issues, you can use the Lighthouse tool in Google Chrome.

Open it by right-clicking on a page, selecting “Inspect → Lighthouse → Analyze page load.”

When I was working on the illustrations for this article, I discovered a small bug on the website.

5. Analysis and Adaptation

Analyzing results and adapting is a crucial step in SEO.

Key steps:

  1. Analyze data: Use Google Analytics or Search Console to find out which pages generate the most traffic. Track changes in keyword positions and CTR (click-through rate).
  2. Update content: Regularly refresh old articles by adding up-to-date information, checking links, and refining keywords. Improve text structure for easier reading.
  3. Adapt to changes: Keep an eye on search engine algorithm updates and adjust your strategy. Experiment with new formats, like short videos or infographics.

Below are keyword data points showing how readers find my Patreon article in Ukrainian.

Analyzing such data helps identify growth opportunities.

For example, if your site frequently appears for a specific query in search (Impressions) but gets few clicks, consider improving the content.

You might need to expand on the topic or provide deeper insights into the query.

Since you’re already showing up in search results, improving the content can lead to more clicks.

Why Creators Need SEO?

Advantages

  1. Free targeted traffic: SEO helps attract people to your site or videos without spending on ads, which is especially useful with a limited budget.
  2. Brand recognition and trust: If your content is easy to find, it builds trust in your brand and makes it more visible.

Disadvantages

  1. Slow results: SEO takes time. Often, noticeable results appear after weeks or even months.
  2. Dependence on algorithm changes: Search engines like Google regularly update their algorithms, which can impact your content’s visibility. However, focusing on quality content usually results in more traffic.

How AI is Changing SEO?

Google is increasingly enhancing search results with AI-optimized answers.

The algorithm analyzes key links, extracts crucial information, and displays a ready answer directly in the search results.

For example, I have an article on how to create an OnlyFans account.

Previously, users would visit my site after searching.

Now Google can display the instructions using my content but without my affiliate link.

This is an important factor to consider:

  1. Ready answers instead of links: Search engines are increasingly showing solutions directly in the results instead of listing links.
  2. Content quality over keywords: Algorithms prioritize valuable content with context, rather than keyword-stuffed text.
  3. Adaptation to new formats: Content should stay relevant and tailored to modern search formats. I’m planning to focus on creating videos.
  4. AI as a helper: Use tools like ChatGPT for reviewing, editing, and testing new ideas.

What’s Next?

SEO helps you stand out without spending on ads.

It’s a long-term investment: results come slowly but last a long time.

The key is balance between optimization and value.

Create content that’s useful for people and understandable for search engines.

What is SEO, and why is it important?

SEO, or Search Engine Optimization, is the process of improving a website’s visibility in search engine results. It helps attract organic traffic, build brand recognition, and increase trust without relying on paid advertisements.

How does SEO work?

SEO involves optimizing a website's content, structure, and backlinks to align with search engine algorithms. This helps search engines understand your site and rank it higher for relevant searches, making it more visible to potential visitors.

What are keywords, and how do they affect SEO?

Keywords are the specific words or phrases people use in search engines to find information. By incorporating relevant keywords naturally into your content, you improve your chances of ranking for those terms and reaching your target audience.

What are the main types of SEO?

SEO can be divided into three primary categories. On-page SEO focuses on optimizing content, titles, and meta tags on your website. Off-page SEO builds authority by earning backlinks from other trusted websites. Technical SEO ensures your website meets performance and security standards, such as fast loading times and mobile optimization.

How do I start with SEO as a beginner?

Starting with SEO requires keyword research to identify what your audience is searching for. Create high-quality content that answers their questions and includes those keywords. Focus on making your website user-friendly, ensuring it’s fast, easy to navigate, and accessible on all devices.

How long does it take to see results from SEO?

SEO is a gradual process, and results often appear within a few weeks to several months, depending on factors like competition and the current state of your website. Patience and consistent effort are key to long-term success.

What tools are available for SEO?

Many tools can help improve your SEO efforts. Google Analytics and Google Search Console are great for tracking performance. Tools like Ahrefs, SEMrush, and Screaming Frog provide insights into keywords, backlinks, and technical issues that may affect your rankings.

What is the difference between organic and paid search results?

Organic search results are unpaid listings that appear based on relevance to the user's query and SEO efforts. Paid search results, on the other hand, are advertisements that appear at the top or bottom of the search engine results page, marked with a small "Ad" label.

How do I optimize my website for SEO?

To optimize your website, focus on creating valuable and well-structured content that addresses your audience's needs. Ensure your site loads quickly, is mobile-friendly, and uses descriptive titles and meta descriptions. Building links to authoritative sites and encouraging others to link to your content also helps.

What are backlinks, and why are they important?

Backlinks are links from other websites pointing to your site. They act as votes of confidence, signaling to search engines that your content is valuable and trustworthy. High-quality backlinks can significantly improve your search engine rankings.

Ця стаття створена, щоб допомогти творцям контенту обрати відповідний інструмент для роботи з запитами користувачів та покращення SEO-стратегії.

Кожному автору важливо знаходити правильні питання, на які варто відповідати, — ті, що справді цікавлять вашу аудиторію.

Розглянемо два популярних інструменти для дослідження ключових слів: AlsoAsked та AnswerThePublic.

Я поясню, як кожен з них допомагає знаходити приховані можливості для контенту, покращувати SEO-оптимізацію та підвищувати вашу експертність в очах пошукових систем.

Чому важливо розуміти запити користувачів?

Знання того, що саме запитує ваша аудиторія, є основою створення успішного контенту.

За моїм досвідом, використання реальних запитів користувачів може значно підвищити CTR та збільшити органічний трафік. У деяких випадках кількість кліків на сайт зростала на 20-30%, а трафік з пошуку збільшувався приблизно на 25%.

Результати можуть відрізнятися в залежності від теми та стратегії.

Коли ви безпосередньо відповідаєте на питання вашої аудиторії, це не лише зміцнює довіру до вашого ресурсу, але й позитивно впливає на SEO — зростає клікабельність та приплив органічних користувачів.

Наведу приклад.

Одна з моїх статей отримала помітне зростання трафіку після того, як я застосував дані з AlsoAsked.

У прикладах я показую результати оптимізації моєї статті про способи заробітку на платформі Fansly.

Що таке AlsoAsked?

‍AlsoAsked — це інструмент, створений для вилучення питань з розділу «People also ask» у Google.

Аналізуючи реальні запити користувачів, AlsoAsked генерує безліч ідей для ключових слів та допомагає виявити прогалини у вашому контенті.

Це дає можливість створювати корисні статті, розділи FAQ або навіть навчальні модулі, які безпосередньо відповідають інтересам вашої аудиторії.

Як працює AlsoAsked?

AlsoAsked надсилає запити до Google і збирає структуровані дані з блоку «People also ask».

Цей процес дозволяє вам:

  • Отримувати ієрархію пов’язаних питань,
  • Візуалізувати кластери схожих запитів,
  • Експортувати результати у форматі CSV для подальшого аналізу.
Така структура допомагає побачити, як одне питання природно переходить в інше — свого роду діалог, який можна відобразити у вашому контенті для логічного та послідовного розкриття теми.

Які основні можливості AlsoAsked?

  • Візуалізація даних: наочні карти пов’язаних питань допомагають одразу виявити ідеї для нового контенту.
  • Кластеризація: схожі запити об’єднуються в групи, що дозволяє комплексно охопити тему та уникнути прогалин у матеріалі.

Що таке AnswerThePublic?

AnswerThePublic застосовує інший підхід, використовуючи дані автозаповнення Google для створення карт питань та ідей для ключових слів.

Він фіксує популярні пошукові запити під час їх введення і перетворює їх на наочне представлення основних тем та підтем.

Такий широкий підхід дозволяє генерувати ідеї для контенту, що виходять за межі конкретних запитів з розділу «People also ask».

Які можливості AnswerThePublic?

  • Візуальні карти питань: організовані схеми питань і фраз допомагають швидко визначити потенційні теми та підтем.
  • Генерація ключових слів: окрім питань, сервіс пропонує пов’язані ключові слова, що допомагає укріпити вашу загальну SEO-стратегію.

Також ви можете переглядати результати в AnswerThePublic у вигляді таблиці.

Що таке хештег?

Хештег — це слово або фраза, перед якими стоїть символ #.

Вони спрощують пошук контенту в соцмережах і стали потужним інструментом для просування.

Наприклад, пости в Instagram з хоча б одним хештегом отримують на 12,6% більше взаємодій, ніж ті, що без них.

У 2024 році хештег #TravelTuesday надихнув тисячі людей ділитися своїми подорожами, збільшуючи популярність туристичного контенту та бронювань.

Але правила гри змінюються кожного року.

Якщо ви створюєте контент — блоги, ілюстрації, дизайн чи навчальні відео — важливо розуміти, як хештеги працюють у 2025 році.

Давайте розглянемо, як отримати з них максимум користі.

Еволюція ролі хештегів

У 2007 році хештеги вперше з'явилися в Twitter як спосіб упорядкування обговорень.

Вони швидко стали інструментом для участі у глобальних дискусіях, відстеження трендів і збільшення охоплення контенту.

Після успіху в Twitter хештеги поширилися на Instagram, Facebook та LinkedIn, адаптуючись до завдань кожної платформи:

  1. Instagram: пошук нового контенту і підвищення видимості.
  2. Facebook: групування обговорень і подій.
  3. LinkedIn: допомога в професійній комунікації.

Творці контенту активно використовують хештеги, щоб залучати аудиторію, підвищувати охоплення та створювати вірусні тренди.

Instagram: від кількості до якості

Хештеги в Instagram залишаються важливим інструментом, але акцент змістився на їхню релевантність.

  • Алгоритми Instagram просувають пости з хештегами, які відповідають недавнім інтересам користувачів, наприклад, #EcoFriendlyArt.
  • Розміщення хештегів: додавайте їх у опис або коментарі, щоб покращити сприйняття і уникнути візуального хаосу.

Приклад успішного брендового хештега

Я допомагав із розвитком соцмереж для художниці Ані Ломакіної.

У неї був YouTube-канал із 300 тисячами підписників, але Instagram розвивався повільно.

Ми придумали хештег #ломакіна_глянь.

Наприкінці відео Аня пропонувала глядачам завдання для малювання.

Вони публікували свої роботи в Instagram із цим хештегом, щоб потрапити у її наступне відео, де вона показувала найкращі результати.

Результат: під цим хештегом опублікували понад 150 тисяч робіт, а акаунт Ані виріс із 10 до 100 тисяч підписників за короткий час.

TikTok: тренди і спільноти

На TikTok хештеги допомагають знаходити контент і об'єднувати користувачів.

  • Спільноти: наприклад, #BookTok об'єднав книголюбів і вплинув на продаж бестселерів.
  • Вірусні теги: такі як #DanceChallenge, забезпечують високий рівень взаємодії.
  • Змішуйте теги: використовуйте як трендові, так і нішеві, наприклад, #SmallCreators, щоб розширити охоплення.

X (колишній Twitter): обговорення в реальному часі

Хештеги на цій платформі — це ключ до участі у живих подіях і трендах.

  • Додавайте їх для пошуку тем і збільшення видимості твітів.
  • Використовуйте хештеги стратегічно, щоб залишатися в центрі актуальних обговорень.

LinkedIn: професійна репутація

LinkedIn робить ставку на точне використання хештегів для професійної комунікації.

  • Галузеві теги, такі як #DigitalMarketing, допомагають знаходити колег та однодумців.
  • Професійні тренди: додавайте хештеги, які демонструють ваш досвід, але уникайте надмірного використання.

Хештеги і SEO: як вони пов’язані

Хештеги в соцмережах працюють як ключові слова в SEO: вони спрощують пошук і допомагають користувачам знаходити ваш контент.

  • Синхронізація з SEO-стратегією збільшує вашу видимість.
  • Релевантність: обирайте хештеги, які відповідають популярним темам та інтересам вашої аудиторії.
  • Брендові хештеги створюють цілісний і впізнаваний образ.

Охоплення на платформах і за їх межами

Хештеги ефективно працюють всередині додатків, але їхній вплив на зовнішні пошукові системи (наприклад, Google) обмежений.

  1. У межах платформ: допомагають користувачам швидко знаходити ваш контент.
  2. Поза платформами: використовуйте SEO, вам може бути корисно ознайомитися з моєю статтею про залучення трафіку з пошукових систем.

  1. Ahrefs Free AI Instagram Hashtag Generator: генерує хештеги, оптимально підходящі для вашого контенту.
  2. KeywordTool.io: допомагає знаходити хештеги для різних платформ, включаючи Instagram і Twitter.
  3. AnswerThePublic або AlsoAsked: пропонують унікальні хештеги на основі популярних пошукових запитів користувачів. Ознайомтеся з моїм гайдом та порівнянням AlsoAsked і AnswerThePublic.

Трендові хештеги спрямовані на широку аудиторію і швидко збільшують видимість. Нішеві хештеги об'єднують конкретні спільноти. Комбінація обох дає найкращі результати.

Як створити унікальний весільний хештег?

Поєднуйте особисті елементи, такі як імена, дати та теми, щоб створити креативні хештеги, наприклад, #SmithWedding2025. Для унікальних ідей також можна скористатися генераторами весільних хештегів.

Чи можуть хештеги покращити SEO мого контенту?

У соцмережах хештеги працюють подібно до ключових слів, покращуючи видимість. Проте їхній вплив на зовнішні пошукові системи, такі як Google, обмежений, тому варто зосередитися на оптимізації всередині платформи.

Які хештеги найкращі для Instagram у 2026 році?

Найефективніші хештеги — це таргетовані й конкретні, наприклад, #EcoFriendlyArt для екологічного контенту або #FoodieLife для кулінарних тем. Важливо, щоб вони відповідали вашій аудиторії та контенту.

Як уникнути тіньового бану через хештеги?

Уникайте заборонених або нерелевантних хештегів, оскільки вони можуть знизити вашу видимість. Ретельно досліджуйте хештеги та переконайтеся, що вони відповідають вашому контенту, щоб підтримувати гарний охоплення.

fieldData.meta-title: llms.txt for Creators: Does It Work? + Setup Guide (2025)
fieldData.meta-description: Learn what llms.txt is, see real results from implementation, and get step-by-step instructions for Webflow and WordPress. Honest assessment included.
fieldData.card-description: No one knows if llms.txt actually works—but one client saw +113% traffic after adding it. Here's the honest truth and how to set it up.
fieldData.post-body:
No one knows if llms.txt actually works—but here's why I use it anyway, and what happened when I added it to my sites.

In September 2024, AI researcher Jeremy Howard proposed a simple idea: give AI systems a clean map of your website's best content. The file is called llms.txt, and it's supposed to help ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and other AI tools understand what your site is about.

I've implemented llms.txt on my own multilingual blog and for clients like united24media.com. The results? Modest but noticeable AI traffic increases—and one site saw +113% traffic in 30 days.

But here's the thing: I can't prove llms.txt caused any of it.

This guide covers what llms.txt actually is, the honest evidence for and against it, and step-by-step implementation for Webflow and WordPress creators.

What is llms.txt?

llms.txt is a simple text file that sits at your website's root (yoursite.com/llms.txt) and tells AI systems what your most important content is.

Think of it as a curated menu for AI crawlers.

While robots.txt tells search engines what they can't access, llms.txt tells AI systems what content is most useful.

It's written in Markdown format—plain text that AI systems process more efficiently than messy HTML full of navigation menus and ads.

‍

The specification was created by Jeremy Howard, co-founder of Answer.AI and former president of Kaggle. His credentials matter: he pioneered transfer learning techniques that contributed to models like GPT. When someone this accomplished proposes a standard, the tech world pays attention.

Here's what a basic llms.txt file looks like:

# Your Site Name
> A one-sentence description of what you do and who you help.
## Main Content
- [Your Best Guide](https://yoursite.com/guide): What this page covers
- [Popular Article](https://yoursite.com/article): Why it's valuable
## Optional
- [Blog Archive](https://yoursite.com/blog): Secondary content

The only required element is the H1 heading with your site name. Everything else—descriptions, link sections, the "Optional" marker—helps AI systems but isn't mandatory.

Here's my llms.txt in action:

Does llms.txt actually work?

Let's be honest: the evidence is genuinely mixed.

What the research says

No major AI company has confirmed they use llms.txt.‍

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Perplexity have all published their own llms.txt files for documentation sites—but none have stated their AI systems read llms.txt files from other websites.

Google's John Mueller compared llms.txt to the "keywords meta tag"—a deprecated standard no search engine uses anymore. He stated: "None of the AI services have said they're using LLMs.txt... and you can tell when you look at your server logs that they don't even check for it."

When website owners check their server logs, results are thin.

SE Ranking's study of 300,000 domains found no correlation between AI citations and llms.txt implementation.

Semrush tested directly: over two months, they observed zero visits from GPTBot, ClaudeBot, or PerplexityBot to llms.txt files.

What I've seen in practice

My experience tells a slightly different story—though I'm careful about claiming causation.

After adding llms.txt to my multilingual blog (English, Ukrainian, Russian), I noticed AI tools started sending more traffic to my English articles specifically. The effect wasn't dramatic, but it was measurable. My theory: the llms.txt file helped AI systems understand which language versions to prioritize.

For a client site—united24media.com—we saw +113% traffic increase in 30 days after implementing llms.txt alongside other optimizations.

Was it the llms.txt file?

Impossible to isolate. But the timing was interesting.

Here's my honest assessment:

‍llms.txt is a helper, not a magic solution. If your content isn't great, llms.txt won't save you. If your content is already good, llms.txt might give AI systems the context they need to find and cite it.

Why implement it anyway?

The risk-reward calculation is simple:

  • Downside: 30 minutes of work
  • Upside: If AI providers eventually adopt the standard, you're already positioned

Over 13,000 websites have implemented llms.txt, with adoption growing roughly 600% between February and May 2025. Notable adopters include Anthropic, Cloudflare, Stripe, and Zapier—all for developer documentation.

For creators targeting developer audiences or using AI coding assistants like Cursor (which explicitly supports llms.txt), the value is clearer. For general content creators, it's a calculated bet on an uncertain standard.

How to create an llms.txt file

Creating your llms.txt file takes about 30 minutes and requires no coding knowledge.

Step 1: Identify your best content

Start by listing your 10-20 most important pages:

  • Your about page
  • Key product or service pages
  • FAQ sections
  • Your best-performing blog posts
  • Any cornerstone content

Don't include your entire site. The point is curation, not completeness.

Step 2: Write the file

Open any text editor and create this structure:

# [Your Site Name]

> [One sentence: What you do + who you help]

[2-3 sentences of additional context about your expertise or approach]

## Core Content
- [Homepage](https://yoursite.com): [What visitors learn here]
- [About](https://yoursite.com/about): [Your background and story]
- [Services](https://yoursite.com/services): [What you offer]

## Resources
- [Best Guide](https://yoursite.com/guide): [Why it's valuable]
- [Popular Article](https://yoursite.com/article): [Key takeaway]

## Optional
- [Blog](https://yoursite.com/blog): [What topics you cover]
- [Contact](https://yoursite.com/contact): [How to reach you]

Step 3: Make descriptions specific

This is where most people fail. Generic descriptions waste your optimization opportunity.

Weak:

[Marketing Services](https://yoursite.com/services): Marketing help

Strong:

[Marketing Services](https://yoursite.com/services): Digital marketing for local restaurants—Google Business Profile optimization, review management, and local SEO

The more specific your descriptions, the better AI systems can match relevant queries.

Step 4: Keep it concise

Keep the file under 3,000 words. AI systems may skip overly long files. Quality over quantity.

Step 5: Validate before publishing

Use free validators to catch errors:

  • llmstxtvalidator.dev
  • llmstxtchecker.net

Check for missing H1 headings, broken links, or formatting issues.

How to add llms.txt to Webflow

Webflow now offers native support for llms.txt.

Method 1: Using the SEO field (recommended)

  1. Go to Site Settings → SEO in your Webflow dashboard
  2. Look for the llms.txt field (Webflow added this dedicated field recently)
  3. Paste your llms.txt content directly
  4. Publish your site

The file will be served from yoursite.com/llms.txt automatically.

Method 2: Using Assets Panel

  1. Create your llms.txt file locally
  2. Go to the Assets Panel in Webflow
  3. Upload the file
  4. Webflow will serve it from your domain root

I use Method 1 because it's easier to update directly in the dashboard without re-uploading files.

How to add llms.txt to WordPress

WordPress has several options depending on your preferred workflow.

Using Yoast SEO (easiest)

If you already use Yoast SEO, they added one-click llms.txt generation in June 2025:

  1. Go to Yoast SEO → Settings → Site Features
  2. Toggle on the llms.txt option
  3. The plugin auto-generates your file weekly, prioritizing cornerstone content

The auto-generated version is a decent starting point, but you may want to customize descriptions for better results.

Using a dedicated plugin

The "Website LLMs.txt" plugin offers more control:

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Go to Settings → LLMs.txt
  3. Write or paste your custom llms.txt content
  4. Save

Manual upload

If you prefer full control:

  1. Create your llms.txt file locally
  2. Connect via FTP or your hosting file manager
  3. Upload to your site's root directory (same folder as wp-config.php)

Common mistakes to avoid

Making the file too long

If your llms.txt is 10,000 words, you've defeated the purpose. AI systems have limited context windows. Include only content that genuinely matters.

Wrong file location

Your file must live at exactly yoursite.com/llms.txt—not in a subdirectory. AI crawlers look for it at the root.

Vague descriptions

"Great content for entrepreneurs" tells AI nothing useful. Specific details about what each page covers help AI systems match relevant queries.

Forgetting to update

If your llms.txt links to pages that no longer exist, AI systems may lose trust in your site's reliability. Schedule quarterly reviews.

Including low-value pages

Exclude checkout flows, user account pages, tag archives, and anything behind authentication. Focus on your best public content.

What about llms-full.txt?

A variant called llms-full.txt contains complete content rather than just links. It was developed by Mintlify in collaboration with Anthropic.

The idea: instead of making AI systems follow URLs to get content, give them everything directly. This is useful for documentation sites where you want AI to have immediate access.

For most content creators, the standard llms.txt with links is sufficient. Use llms-full.txt only if you specifically want AI systems to have your complete content without crawling.

Alternatives that definitely work today

While llms.txt remains speculative, proven AI optimization methods exist:

Structured data (Schema.org)

Schema markup helps AI systems understand your content's context—what type it is, who created it, when it was published. Unlike llms.txt, structured data is actively used by Google's AI systems. Add FAQ schema, Article schema, and HowTo schema where relevant.

Answer-first content structure

AI systems love content that directly answers questions. Start each section with a clear answer in 40-60 words, then expand. This structure helps both AI Overviews and traditional featured snippets.

Traditional SEO excellence

Many AI tools pull answers from search results. The same SEO fundamentals that help Google understand your content—clean heading hierarchy, short paragraphs, direct answers—also help AI systems find your best work.

The bottom line

llms.txt is a 30-minute investment with uncertain but potentially significant upside. No major AI company has confirmed they use it, but adoption is growing and the specification comes from a credible source.

My approach: implement it, but don't obsess over it. The file takes minimal effort to create and maintain. If AI providers eventually standardize on llms.txt, you'll be ahead. If they don't, you've lost almost nothing.

Focus on what definitely works—great content, clear structure, proper schema markup—and treat llms.txt as one small piece of your AI discoverability strategy. That's all!

Frequently Asked Questions
fieldData.faq:
Do AI crawlers actually read llms.txt files?

No major AI company has confirmed their systems read llms.txt. Server log analyses show mixed results—some sites report increased AI crawler activity, others see no change. The honest answer: we don't know for certain.

Is llms.txt the same as robots.txt?

No. robots.txt tells crawlers what they can't access. llms.txt tells AI systems what content is most useful—it's curation, not restriction. They serve different purposes and both can exist on your site.

Should I implement llms.txt if I'm just starting out?

If your content isn't great yet, llms.txt won't help. Focus on creating genuinely useful content first. Once you have 10-20 strong pages worth curating, then consider llms.txt.

How often should I update my llms.txt file?

Review quarterly, or whenever you publish major new content. Remove broken links and add your newest important pages. Outdated llms.txt files with dead links may hurt more than help.

Does llms.txt help with Google rankings?

Google has explicitly stated they don't use llms.txt and have no plans to support it. llms.txt is for AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity—not traditional search engines.
